sources.entry: Strix - Auto-discovers working stream URLs for IP cameras and generates ready-to-use Frigate and go2rtc configs. MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Strix is a camera stream discovery tool that finds working stream URLs for IP cameras and generates Frigate and go2rtc configs.
summary.what_it_does: Strix probes a camera IP for open ports, MAC vendor, mDNS/HomeKit and HTTP server details. You search for the camera model in its SQLite database of 3,600+ brands and 100,000+ URL patterns, optionally entering credentials. It then builds candidate stream URLs from those patterns and tests them with 20 parallel workers, collecting live screenshots, codecs, resolution and latency. You pick main and sub streams from the results and get a ready Frigate config that can be copied, downloaded, or saved directly into Frigate. It also auto-discovers Frigate and go2rtc on the local network and smart-merges into an existing setup. Supported protocols listed are RTSP, RTSPS, HTTP/HTTPS (MJPEG, snapshots, HLS, MPEG-TS), RTMP, Bubble, DVRIP and HomeKit.
use_cases: discover RTSP stream URL for an IP camera
set up go2rtc streams for cameras
find camera model stream paths in a database
test which camera URLs actually work
add IP cameras to a home NVR setup
how_to_run: bash <install script from README; the command was cut off in the source, so see the README>
docker run -d --name strix --network host --restart unless-stopped eduard256/strix:latest
notable: Camera stream database of 3,600+ brands and 100,000+ URL patterns, maintained separately in StrixCamDB
Auto-discovery of Frigate and go2rtc on the local network
Tests every candidate URL with 20 parallel workers and live screenshots
Zero-dependency static binary for Linux amd64/arm64
Exposes an HTTP API for integration into smart home platforms
caveats: Network scanning needs NET_RAW and NET_ADMIN capabilities (or privileged mode) under Podman
Binary install requires ffmpeg for screenshot conversion
Binary releases are published for Linux amd64/arm64 only
